meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'there', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There is a complex formula there.

examples.text: В суши отвези, там с руками оторвут.
examples.trans: Take it to a sushi place, they will snatch it right up there.

examples.text: Там вкус был такой терпкий, приятный, природный.
examples.trans: There the taste was so tart, pleasant, natural.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ложный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('complex, complicated').

examples.trans: There is a complex formula there.
Look, there's nothing complicated.
That's a very difficult question.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'formula' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There is a complex formula there.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть формула.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always formula.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, near, with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Эффектная подача блюд делает их вкуснее.
examples.trans: Spectacular presentation of dishes makes them tastier.
An individual approach?
In my opinion, the main thing is patience.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'us', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Навоза? Ну, в смысле дать? Купи!
examples.trans: Manure? What do you mean, give? Buy it!

examples.text: Ребёнку необходимы белки, которые есть только в мясе.
examples.trans: A baby needs proteins that are only in meat.
We didn't see anything.

meanings.en: to appear, to show up, to turn up
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'явиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to appear, to show up', paired with 'появляться'.

examples.text: Пусть только ещё раз здесь появится!
examples.trans: Let him just show up here one more time!
We came up with a good idea.

examples.text: Я тебе серьёзно говорю. Пусть только ещё раз здесь появится!
examples.trans: I'm telling you seriously. Let him just show up here one more time!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'else/more', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: У нас появился ещё один шутник.
examples.trans: We have got ourselves another prankster.

examples.text: От вас муж ещё не ушёл?
examples.trans: Hasn't your husband left you yet?

examples.text: Мало того, что она меня чуть не задавила, она меня ещё оскорбляла.
examples.trans: Not only did she almost run me over, she also insulted me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian cardinal or ordinal numeral meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Everyone works, not just you alone.
Redhead, wait.

examples.text: У нас появился ещё один шутник.
examples.trans: We have got ourselves another prankster.

meanings.note: Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'joker, prankster' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: У нас появился ещё один шутник.
examples.trans: We have got ourselves another prankster.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть шутник.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always joker.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: I felt like having a little apple.

examples.text: Ты нас хотела отравить? Накормила нас!
examples.trans: Did you want to poison us? She fed us that!

examples.text: Ты что хотел сказать? Нагиев оказал медвежью услугу.
examples.trans: What did you want to say? Nagiyev did us a disservice.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'war' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Хочешь войны? Будет тебе торпеда в борт.
examples.trans: Do you want war? You will get a torpedo to the hull.

examples.text: Макс, чего ты твой столик не забрал?
examples.trans: Max, why didn't you take your table?

examples.text: В прошлый раз я думала, война началась.
examples.trans: Last time I thought a war had started.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'will be'.

examples.text: Шеф, дорогой, для тебя я могу быть кем угодно.
examples.trans: Chef, my dear friend, for you I can be anyone at all.
First of all, it must be fresh.
I have a toy car.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты что делаешь? Заказал просто кофе!
examples.trans: What are you doing? He ordered just coffee!

examples.text: Сегодня по семь тысяч. Не густо.
examples.trans: Seven thousand each today. Not much.

examples.text: Почему я должен работать на ушастых?
examples.trans: Why do I have to work for big-eared rookies?

examples.text: Что самое важное в работе официанта?
examples.trans: What is the most important thing in a waiter's job?

examples.text: Эффектная подача блюд делает их вкуснее.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'board, hull' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Хочешь войны? Будет тебе торпеда в борт.
examples.trans: Do you want war? You will get a torpedo to the hull.

examples.text: Наша жизнь — это всегда результат нашего выбора.
examples.trans: Our life is always the result of our choice.
Time will show our choice!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спорим на все чаевые за смену?
examples.trans: Shall we bet all the tips for the shift?

examples.trans: And here, keep the change.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hello (on the phone)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello, how are things?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello, how are things?

examples.text: Молодой, красивый, умный, как мой племянник.
examples.trans: Young, handsome, smart, just like my nephew.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'things to do' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Эффектная подача блюд делает их вкуснее.

examples.trans: Nothing special.

examples.text: А ты таким голосом его и пугал?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Nothing special.

examples.text: Иду, иду. Чего ты ржёшь? Ничего.
examples.trans: I am going, I am going. Why are you laughing? Nothing.

examples.text: Если так будешь разговаривать, вообще ничего не получишь.
examples.trans: If you talk like that, you will get nothing at all.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'when', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: When do you fly in? Tomorrow?

examples.text: Когда закончилась смена. Правильно? Это что?
examples.trans: When the shift has ended. Right? What is this?

examples.text: Что будет, когда Дима узнает, что он съел?
examples.trans: What will happen when Dima finds out what he ate?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'летать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'arrive by plane'.

related.gloss: not to arrive by plane (negated infinitive)

examples.trans: When do you fly in? Tomorrow?

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и прилетать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and arrive by plane on time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.trans: When do you fly in? Tomorrow?
I didn't have breakfast today.

examples.text: А если мне завтра что-нибудь другое захочется?
examples.trans: And what if tomorrow I feel like having something else?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Эффектная подача блюд делает их вкуснее.
examples.trans: Spectacular presentation of dishes makes them tastier.

examples.text: Так, это мне нельзя. Это тоже.
examples.trans: Right, I am not allowed to have this. This either.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Nagiyev gave me a surprise here.

examples.text: Вёз взятку в институт, а он сам сессию закрыл.
examples.trans: I was bringing a bribe to the institute, and he passed the exams himself.
I'm here.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'юрприз'). Common masculine noun meaning 'surprise' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Nagiyev gave me a surprise here.
I'll show you one surprise.
What surprise?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'made', paired with 'делать'.

examples.trans: Nagiyev gave me a surprise here.
Fedya, make me a sandwich, will you?

examples.text: Ну да, из чего сделала, то и получилось.
examples.trans: Well yes, what I made it from is what it turned out to be.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'arrive', paired with 'приезжать'.

examples.trans: Which car did you come in?
Pasha has arrived.

examples.text: Вика, ты на какой машине сегодня приехала?
examples.trans: Vika, which car did you come in today?

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'сказать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will tell', paired with 'рассказывать'.

examples.trans: Tell me what happened.
I'll tell Mum everything.
Tell that to Stalin.

meanings.note: Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'звонить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will call back', paired with 'перезванивать'.

examples.trans: I'll call you back.
Call me back tonight.
A lucky break: Tretyakov called back.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Knock it off right now!
Everyone get to work right now!

examples.text: Замени на что-нибудь другое, сделай быстро.
examples.trans: Replace it with something else, make it quickly.

meanings.en: to stop, put an end to
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'stopped, knock it off', paired with 'прекращать'.

examples.trans: Knock it off right now!
Stop it! We will have the flat.
Stop making noise!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to work', paired with 'поработать'.

examples.text: Почему я должен работать на ушастых?
examples.trans: Why do I have to work for big-eared rookies?
What? Do I not work?
Everyone works, not just you alone.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to everyone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Eva — five thousand two hundred.
Everything's fine.
As you all know...
